episodes.210792: An strong upper-level low with an associated surface cold front allowed to ample lift in an environment with sufficient shear and instability for a line of showers and isolated thunderstorms to form during the afternoon and evening hours of March 13, 2026. Strong-to-damaging wind gusts were observed across northwestern Pennsylvania with these features with the most widespread wind damage in portions of Clearfield County during the late afternoon to early evening hours.
episodes.212211: Precip amounts of 2 to 2.5 inches fell in the Palouse area from March 13 through the 14. It led to flooding in the City of Pullman.
episodes.212213: Precip amounts of 2 to 2.5 inches fell in the Palouse area from March 13 through the 14. It led to flooding in the City of Moscow.
episodes.212345: Heavy snow in the northern Blue mountains transitioned to rain the night of the 13th through the 14th, leading to rises in area rivers and streams. Portions of the Touchet river and Mill Creek eventually exceeded their banks, leading to flooding of residential areas and roadways across Columbia and Walla Walla Counties.

events.narrative: A line of showers producing wind gusts estimated at 60 mph knocked multiple trees down onto South Eagle Valley Road approximately 5 miles northwest of Park Forest.

Several areas across Moscow had localized flooding issues. Areas included Berman Creekside Park, Soccer fields on west side of Guy Wicks Field, Mountain View Roundabout, White Avenue and Highway 8, Damen Street, Lemhi Drive, North Couplet of Main Street, Perimeter Drive at Pullman Highway, Sand Road outside of Moscow, and the city park along the Potlatch River.

South Fork Palouse River flooding, with minor to moderate flooding in areas across Pullman, including downtown, Grand Avenue, and the area around the City Playfields. Water covered N Grand north of NW Windus St. NE Morton St by Reaney pool was flooded across all lanes. Grand Avenue closed from Nye to Ritchie. Main Street from Spring to Pine was closed. Morton Street near Reaney Park closed due to flooding.

The Columbia County Emergency Managers office reported flooding of residences and water over roadways in the town of Dayton the morning of the 14th. Drone footage over Dayton taken on the 14th showed the Touchet river overflowing it's banks into numerous properties adjacent to the river, with flooding also along the Patit Creek that runs through the northern portion of Dayton.

The Walla Walla County dispatch reported flooding along the Touchet River in the town of Waitsburg the morning of the 14th. The dispatch center relayed that a levee near the Preston Ave bridge had been breached, leading to flooding of properties along the Touchet River. Several roads in the Waitsburg area were also closed, including US Highway 12, due to water over the roadway.
